data.name: Sereniah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew words 'seren' (peace) and 'yah' (God). The name Sereniah means 'divine healing' or 'peaceful one from God'. In biblical contexts, it could refer to a serene and healing presence of God.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine healing and peace in times of spiritual need.

in_hebrew.name: סרניה
in_hebrew.meaning: ה׳ שמע ועניתי (Hashem Shama V'Oneni) - אלוהים שמע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סרניה הוא שם עברי שמקורו בשם העברי סרניהו, שפירושו 'אלוהים שמע' או 'ה׳ שמע ועניתי'. השם מורכב מהמילים 'סרן' שפירושו 'שר' או 'גדול', ו'-יה' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם נמצא בספר עזרא, פרק 2, פסוק 55, ובספר נחמיה, פרק 7, פסוק 57, כחלק משמות הכהנים ששבתו מירושלים לבבל.

in_greek.name: Σερενίας
in_greek.meaning: Θεός άκροατής (Theos akroates) - ο Θεός ακούει
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σερενίας προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα Σרניהו (Sereniahu), που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός ακούει' ή 'Θεός άκροατής'. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα σχετίζεται με την έννοια της προσευχής και της επικοινωνίας με τον Θεό. Στη Βίβλο, το όνομα εμφανίζεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη ως μέρος των ονομάτων των ιερέων που επέστρεψαν από την εξορία.

in_latin.name: Sereniah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sereniah origine hebraeo, Sereniahu, quod significat 'Deus exaudit' vel 'Deus audit'. In traditione christiana, nomen hoc habet significationem orationis et communicationis cum Deo. In scripturis sacris, nomen invenitur in libro Ezrae et Nehemiae, inter nomina sacerdotum qui a captivitate Babylonica redierunt.

in_english.name: Sereniah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sereniah originates from the Hebrew name Sereniahu, meaning 'God hears' or 'God listened'. It is derived from the Hebrew words 'sar' meaning 'chief' or 'prince' and 'yah' meaning 'God'. The name appears in the Bible in Ezra 2:55 and Nehemiah 7:57, referring to a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile. In Christian tradition, the name symbolizes the power of prayer and divine attention. It is associated with spiritual significance, humility, and devotion.

historical_references.reference: An early Christian martyr named Sereniah is mentioned in the 'Acts of the Martyrs of Lyons and Vienne'. This work recounts the persecutions of Christians in Gaul during the reign of Marcus Aurelius (161-180 AD). Sereniah is one of the seven deacons who are martyred for their faith.

The 'Golden Legend' or 'Legenda Aurea' by Jacobus de Voragine, a medieval collection of hagiographic texts, includes a brief biography of Saint Serenia. According to this text, she was a wealthy Roman woman who devoted her life to caring for the sick and the poor. She was eventually discovered, arrested, and put on trial for her Christian faith during the reign of Diocletian (284-305 AD). Despite being tortured and threatened, she refused to renounce her faith and was eventually executed.
